slides.heading: The Print Statement
slides.body: The Print Statement is part of Introduction to Python and Output. This short lesson gives you a practical Python idea you can understand, try, and reuse in simple programs.

slides.heading: Core Idea: The Print Statement
slides.body: The print() function displays text or values on the screen. It is one of the first tools new programmers use because it immediately shows what the program is doing.

slides.heading: Real-World Analogy
slides.body: Using print() is like speaking through a microphone. Whatever message you place inside it becomes visible to the audience.

annotations.note: This line displays a value or message on the screen.

slides.heading: Key Rule
slides.body: Write one clear instruction at a time. Python reads your code from top to bottom, so order and spelling matter.

slides.heading: Try It Yourself!
slides.prompt: Print the message Ready to learn!
slides.hint: Place the message inside quotation marks.

quiz.prompt_text: What does the print() function do in Python?

options: Stores a value in memory for later use
Displays text or values on the screen
Asks the user to enter some information

quiz.explanation: Exactly right! print() displays whatever you put inside it on the screen — it is one of the first tools every Python programmer learns.

quiz.prompt_text: Arrange the following lines of code in the correct order to print the message 'Welcome to MyADA'.
quiz.explanation: The comment explaining what we are doing goes first, then the print() statement runs to show the message on the screen.

quiz.prompt_text: Write a program that prints the message 'Ready to learn!' on the screen.

content.hint: Place the message inside quotation marks: print("Ready to learn!").

quiz.correct_answer: Any valid Python code that satisfies the prompt.
quiz.explanation: Write print("Ready to learn!") — the text inside the quotes is exactly what Python will display on the screen.
